title: Sheaf tensor with an ideal quotient, normalized on sections and quotient maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal subsheaf (a subsheaf stable under multiplication by local sections of $R$). For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $IF\subseteq F$ be the subsheaf whose sections are locally finite sums $\sum_a i_af_a$, with $i_a\in I$ and $f_a\in F$ on the members of a covering sieve. Put $S=R/I$ and $Q_I(F)=F/IF$, with quotients formed by sheafifying the sectionwise quotients [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Use sheaf tensor and its pure sections [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Then $Q_I(F)$ has its canonical $S$-module structure, and there is an $S$-linear isomorphism
$$a_{I,F}:F\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_I(F),\qquad f\otimes\bar r\longmapsto[rf],\qquad a_{I,F}^{-1}([f])=f\otimes1.$$
These formulas mean identities on images of local sections in the sheafifications. Writing $q_{I,F}:F\to Q_I(F)$ and $u_{I,F}:F\to F\otimes_RS$ for $f\mapsto[f]$ and $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, one has $a_{I,F}u_{I,F}=q_{I,F}$; in particular $u_{I,F}$ is an epimorphism with kernel $IF$. For any $R$-linear sheaf morphism $h:F\to G$, the induced quotient map $Q_I(h)([f])=[h(f)]$ satisfies
$$Q_I(h)a_{I,F}=a_{I,G}(h\otimes1).$$
For any ideal subsheaf $I'\subseteq I$, let $t:R/I'\to R/I$ and $v:Q_{I'}(F)\to Q_I(F)$ be the quotient maps. After restriction to $R$-modules,
$$v\,a_{I',F}=a_{I,F}(1_F\otimes t),\qquad (1_F\otimes t)u_{I',F}=u_{I,F}.$$
No flatness of $F$, existence of points, or surjectivity of $R(U)\to S(U)$ on every object is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification of the tensor-quotient balanced maps; the quotient identification and its two naturality squares are the agent-written extraction of the original item steps 2–5.

proof.text: Use Mathlib locally surjective and locally injective sheafification maps. The cokernel projection is sectionwise surjective, so its composite with sheafification is locally surjective. For commutative rings, the quotient projection followed by ring sheafification is likewise locally surjective. The imageSieve and equalizerSieve APIs provide covering sieves of representatives and equalities; no precoverage or fibre products are required.

source.place: Tags 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures) and 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); module identification from Tag 03CY

proof.text: Construct the sectionwise ideal-product submodule. Its local hull consists of sections whose membership sieve covers. Intersections of covers give addition, restrictions give scalar stability, and transitivity gives saturation. This hull equals the intersection defining localProduct. A saturated subfunctor of a sheaf is a sheaf. Submodule.smul_induction_on identifies the sectionwise ideal product with finite sums. Evaluate the cokernel as the quotient by the inclusion range; local injectivity of sheafification and saturation identify the kernel of q. Local representatives and separatedness prove q is epic.

source.place: Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), applied to the sheafified module quotient; local ideal-product argument written out here

proof.text: The ideal annihilates the already sheafified quotient Q: locally lift a section to f and use q(if)=0; separatedness proves the assertion globally. Module.IsTorsionBySet.module consequently gives Q an action of the quotient ring presheaf S0. Apply PresheafOfModules.sheafify to S0→S and the identity of the underlying abelian sheaf Q. Its canonical map proves compatibility with the original R-action and supplies the identity-on-sections R-linear isomorphism e.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), applied to the quotient ring presheaf and its module quotient

proof.text: Define B(f,s)=s q(f) using the constructed S-action. The scalar compatibility gives R-bilinearity. TensorProduct.lift constructs a morphism on tensor presheaves, and the module sheafification adjunction extends it to a on the actual sheaf tensor. The adjunction unit and tensor/sheafification comparison give a(pure(f,s))=s q(f).

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor followed by sheafification; local representatives justified by the cited local-section theorem

proof.text: Define u(f)=pure(f,1) using pureBilin and pure_restrict. Balancing and the vanishing of ideal elements under ringProjection show u(if)=0. The finite-sum description and separatedness show that u kills localProduct. The cokernel universal property and sheafification adjunction give b with qb=u.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), tensor balancing and descent through the quotient presheaf

proof.text: The pure-section formula gives ua=q. Cancel the epic q to prove ba=1 on Q. To prove ab=1 on the tensor, use pure_hom_ext and a covering imageSieve on which s lifts to r. There b(a(pure(f,s)))=b(q(rf))=pure(rf,1)=pure(f,s); separatedness concludes. Multiplicativity of the S-action proves the scalar-linearity clause directly from a(pure(f,s))=s q(f).

proof.text: The projection identity and the isomorphism give u=q b, hence epimorphy of u. Apply a and b to show u(f)=0 iff q(f)=0, and use the quotient kernel computed above.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), elementary consequences of the constructed inverse and the quotient kernel from step 2

proof.text: For h:F→G, define qh by conjugating h tensor id with the comparison isomorphisms. Naturality of pure sections gives u_F followed by h tensor id = h followed by u_G, hence the quotient-projection square. The locally surjective coefficient projection makes restriction of scalars fully faithful on sheaves; lift the R-linear qh across e to its S-linear hS. The tensor square is the isomorphism identity.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), agent-written naturality calculation for module morphisms

proof.text: For I′ contained in I, naturality of ring sheafification proves ringProjection_I′ followed by ringTransition = ringProjection_I. Thus ringTransition defines the required R-linear coefficient map tM. Its value on 1 and pure_map prove the unit-transition identity. Define v by conjugating id tensor tM with a_I′ and a_I; the unit identity gives the quotient-projection square, and inverse cancellation gives the tensor square.
